claim: The eight sdlc-* skills now have one replacement to be judged against: sov-lifecycle, an instance of the portable core see-it-through in the bdos repository, pinned by digest and refused by a checker when it drifts. It carries the whole path a concern takes and cites every rule to the document that owns it. What needs your judgement is the one thing this session could not do: SDLC.md, Skill axes, declares those eight skills by name and states an operator holds exactly one tier skill plus its domain skills, so the tree cannot drop them without that section changing, and SDLC.md is excluded from the standing grant. Until you rule, the repository holds nine skills covering the same ground, which is more duplication than before and not less. Five changed paths sit outside the standing grant and ride this branch rather than landing under it: STATUS.yaml and ROADMAP.md, which the grant does not reach; acceptance/A25.json, this packet; .clarity/coverage.json; and reports/context/baseline.json. CLAUDE.md is no longer among them - main deleted the hardcoded counts this branch was correcting, which removes the drift rather than resetting it, so both corrections are withdrawn as obsolete.

visible_result.shows: the orientation snapshot agreeing with the record once CLAUDE.md says 32 skills rather than 31
visible_result.expect: PASS: 9 of 10 snapshot claim(s) match the record. Before the CLAUDE.md line moved this read FAIL skills: page says 31, record holds 32, and scripts/verify.py exited 1. The count moved because .claude/skills/sov-lifecycle/ is the 32nd skill.

evidence.says: the instance: nine stations from taking up a concern to landing it, every rule cited to AGENTS.md, SDLC.md, CLAUDE.md or a contract, and nine refusals. It pins bdos core see-it-through by that core's artifact digest.

Skill axes declares Control, Orchestration, Worker, Product, Development, QA, Release and Feedback skills by name and states that a working operator holds exactly one tier skill and the domain skills its concern requires. Bindings states the loop is stack-neutral and that a second, materially different binding must be able to run it against the same documents. Release gate item 6 states that a Red operator receives the contract, the claimed invariants and the artifact, and never uses the builder's tests or plan as evidence or as the oracle.

Both witness prompts once opened with the orchestrator's operation sentence, which is the oracle position SDLC.md Release gate 6 forbids. That is repaired on this branch: one witnessFrame builds both paths, the builder's account arrives labelled as artifact after the contract and the checks, and eleven sibling workflows were repaired the same way. Line numbers are deliberately absent - the citation that named lines 270 to 283 was stale within one commit.

line 218 filters skill directories on the sdlc- prefix and derives the chart from SDLC.md. Removing the eight fails four charting tests, measured in a throwaway copy: 14 passed at baseline, 4 failed and 10 passed with them removed.
line 118 instructs an agent to read .claude/skills/sdlc-feedback/SKILL.md. A live route to one of the eight, which an earlier reading in this session wrongly reported as absent.

the twenty-three files under .claude/workflows/ assemble every prompt this repository sends an agent and were graded by nothing: lint's suffix set holds no .js. This reads their bytes for CRLF and for the 'a' + + 'b' shape that reached a landing during this work. Three further checks were written and withdrawn because without expression context a reader cannot tell a regex literal from division, and that ceiling is recorded in the module rather than implied.

both were unparseable JavaScript and are repaired here. sov-trust.js closed a string on the apostrophe in "workflow's"; sov-coldstart.js held three strings broken across raw newlines. Both are documented launch paths and both would have failed at load. They were broken before this work and were reported clean by its first workflow check, which is the finding: a false all-clear is worse than the silence it replaced. scripts/sovharness/lexer.py now reads them, and node agrees on all twenty-three.

why_it_matters: A rule the repository has held since day two - that an independent reading works from the contract and never from the builder's plan - is stated in SDLC.md and enforced nowhere, and the harness workflow that runs the loop violates it. The eight skills that restate the rule are unreachable, so the statement survived where nothing could act on it. sov-lifecycle puts the whole path in one place with the rule cited at the station where it applies, and being an instance rather than a local skill means a second harness can bind the same core rather than writing a ninth version. The duplication this leaves is real and is the reason the packet exists: the replacement cannot supersede the eight while SDLC.md declares them.
what_could_defeat_it: A ruling that the eight tier and domain skills are the right shape and one path skill is the wrong one, in which case sov-lifecycle should be withdrawn rather than the eight retired.
An operator that genuinely needs to load exactly one tier's competence without the rest of the path, which is what Skill axes currently assumes and what one path skill cannot serve.
Evidence that binding to a core in another repository costs more than it saves, since nothing in this repository runs the grader and the pin is checked only where bdos is.
A second harness that cannot express the core's kernel, which would make stack-neutrality a claim this instance does not actually demonstrate.
residuals: The eight sdlc-* skills remain, so nine skills now cover the same ground. That is the judgement this packet asks for and the reason it is presented rather than landed.
Nothing in this repository runs python -m bdos instance, so the pinned digest cannot report a moved core from here. The skill states this rather than implying it.
No skill's clarity basis includes SDLC.md, so sov-lifecycle's promise that SDLC.md prevails on divergence has no staleness detector: if SDLC.md moves, nothing stales the skill.

The independent judge dissented on the first pass and its findings are repaired in this commit, including a blocking one: verify.py passed against the working tree and failed against the commit, because snapshot claims that read committed bytes cannot see an uncommitted file. The evidence was gathered against a state that was not the state landed.

Appending one acceptance-queue entry to STATUS.yaml staled 60 clarity readers, because STATUS.yaml is their declared basis and the basis is the whole file. The reading each needed was one question - does a queued packet change what this document must satisfy - answered no for all 60 before re-stamping, and the previous packet-queuing commit did the same. That is sanctioned rather than correct: a basis that stales everything on a queue movement makes staleness mean less each time, which is the erosion contracts/clarity.json exists to prevent. Scoping a basis below whole-file is a separate concern in the contracts boundary.

The witness-context defect this work names is repaired on this branch, in sov-loop.js and eleven sibling workflows, with scripts/tests/test_witness_context_provenance.py refusing its return. An independent reading defeated the first version of that check five ways and it was rewritten to render the prompt rather than grade its source text; the second reading is not yet in.

A packet's evidence addresses carry null digests and nothing grades them for staleness, so this packet's own citation to sov-loop.js went false within one commit and no check noticed. That is a gap in the acceptance surface, not in this work.

SUPERSEDED, kept as history: The workflow reader grades two byte-level shapes and nothing about meaning. Bracket balance, prose-stripped source, and a count of dispatches naming no agentType were each written and withdrawn after being defeated by this repository's own files. A real reading of these workflows needs a JavaScript parser, which crosses the dependency boundary ENGINEERING.md governs and is a separate concern for the owner rather than something to smuggle in under a test.

The claim that bracket balance and string termination could not be graded without a JavaScript parser was refuted by an independent reading and is withdrawn. It was convenient rather than true, and while it stood, two dead workflows were certified clean by a check and by a green test. The lexer that replaces it states its own limit: a grammar error whose tokens are all well formed still passes.

Current reading of the workflow surface, replacing the superseded entry above: scripts/sovharness/lexer.py reads every workflow as JavaScript - strings close, brackets match - and node reads the same bytes as a module where an engine is present, which catches a grammar error whose tokens are all well formed. `node --check` on a .js does not: these files open with `export` and it returns zero whatever they contain, which is why two unparseable workflows survived a hand-run check. Where no engine exists the run prints that the grammar went unread rather than passing over it.

The operational landing ledger held 156 rows of test traffic, written through the import-time root binding in scripts/sov_land.py. Repairing that is on this branch. The rows themselves were destroyed during the repair: the first form of the isolation test computed the ledger path from the effective root and wrote to it, which under the defect it was written to detect is the operational ledger. They are gitignored with no committed history and are not recoverable. .local/landing/ledger.quarantined.ndjson records the loss, how it happened and what was in them; the test now asserts the path and writes nothing.

Rebased onto current main after being thirty-five commits behind. Three repairs this branch made were already made there by other sessions - the shard-packing assertion, and CLAUDE.md's two hardcoded counts - and upstream's are kept. scripts/sovharness/ collided with PR #233, which declares that package for a different purpose and is based on current main; this branch's package is renamed to scripts/sovprompts/. None of this work is on #233, and #233's CANDIDATE_HISTORY_NONLINEAR refusal belongs to its own branch rather than to anything here.
on_accept: CLAUDE.md carries both corrected counts, sov-lifecycle stands as the declared path at PROPOSED, and the next bounded concern is SDLC.md Skill axes: whether one instance plus domain competences replaces one tier skill plus domain skills. Retiring the eight then follows, with charting/derive.py and sov-compression.js repaired in the same concern because both route to them. The engineering repairs on this branch - the witness frame and its check, the workflow reader, the landing-gate refusals, and the ledger isolation - stand on their own and do not wait on that ruling.
on_reject: Reset claude/witness-context-discovery-runas1 to origin/main. The branch is ten commits, rebased linear onto current main with no merge commits, and reaches well beyond .claude/: it adds scripts/sov_context.py, scripts/sov_workflows.py, scripts/sov_ledger_quarantine.py and the scripts/sovprompts/ package; it changes scripts/sov_land.py, scripts/sovkernel/authority.py, scripts/sovland/ledger.py, scripts/sovverify/integrity.py, twelve workflows, four agents, ROADMAP.md, STATUS.yaml, scripts/README.md, two diagrams and the generated docs page. An earlier revision of this packet said no code outside .claude/ changed; that was true when written and is not true now. No operation became reachable, no service gained an implementation and no standing entry moved. Four repairs would be lost that are independent of the judgement asked here and worth keeping on their own: two unparseable workflows, the import-time root binding that let verification write into operational accounting, the witness frame and its check, and the landing gate's measurable refusals. The bdos half is a separate repository and is unaffected.
